info.title: Media Resource Manager API
info.description:
Self-service management API for MRM cloud workstations: EC2 workstation lifecycle, users and groups, AMIs and Image Builder pipelines, the software library, FSx/S3 storage, DataSync, regional hubs and Amazon DCV sessions.

All routes except `POST /auth/ldap` and `GET /auth/validate` require a bearer token. See `docs/API.md` for how to obtain one.

Generated from the deployed API by `openapi/build.py`; schemas are maintained by hand in `openapi/overlay.json`.

servers.description: Resolve restApiId and region from SSM /{PascalCaseName}/Workstation/ApiUrl, or run `. scripts/mrm-env.sh` and read $MRM_API_URL.

restApiId.description: The deployment's API Gateway REST API id.

bearerAuth.description: A custom Lambda authorizer validates the token. It accepts an HS256 token signed with the deployment's JWT secret, or a Cognito RS256 ID token.

The references reach the real AWS resources as CloudFormation stack tags when the resource is created, so editing one here changes the MRM record and not the tags on a filesystem that already exists.

status.description: Step Functions' own word for the build: RUNNING means it is still going, and any other value is terminal.

output.description: The execution's result, present only when it SUCCEEDED. A failed execution has none; `error` and `cause` are what describe it.

error.description: Step Functions' name for what ended a terminal execution, e.g. `VcpuLimitExceeded`. Null while RUNNING and on success. Not to be confused with the `error` field on this endpoint's 400/404/500 bodies, which reports a fault in the call rather than in the build.

cause.description: The detail behind `error`, passed through verbatim. Usually a JSON document with `errorType`, `errorMessage` and `trace` where a Lambda threw; a bare string where Step Functions itself failed the state. Null while RUNNING and on success.

NotFound.description: Resource not found, or the path/method fell through the handler's router.

POST /auth/ldap.description: Public. Returns an HS256 JWT valid for one hour.

GET /auth/validate.summary: Validate a token (not usable as built)
GET /auth/validate.description: Reads the token from an `auth-token` cookie that no client sets, so this always returns 401. See docs/API.md#known-quirks.

GET /workstations.description: Admins see every workstation; other callers see only those assigned to them or to a group they belong to.

403.description: Feature disabled and caller is not an admin.

POST /dcv.description: One endpoint for nine actions; see docs/API.md#dcv. Requests naming a workstation in another region are forwarded to that region's Lambda.

GET /workstations/orphans.summary: Find instances a create may have leaked
GET /workstations/orphans.description: Instances carrying a ConstellationId tag, split into those MRM has a record of and those it does not. A create tags the instance in the same call that launches it but writes its record afterwards, so anything that kills the function in between leaves a running machine no listing can show. Terminated instances are excluded: one is evidence a build happened, not something to adopt or clean up.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: Where to look. Defaults to the primary region; a build targeted at a regional hub placed its instance elsewhere.

GET /workstations/executions.summary: Read the state of one workstation-creation execution
GET /workstations/executions.description: POST /workstations answers with an executionArn and no instance id, and nothing stores that ARN elsewhere, so this is how a caller that kept it asks what became of the work. A failed execution has no output: `error` and `cause` carry Step Functions' own reason, which is the only account of why a build failed that leaves this API. A terminal status does not settle whether an instance leaked: the instance id enters the execution history only when the create function returns, and the window that leaks one is the window where it never does. GET /workstations/orphans answers that.
